en.name: Corporales de Daroca
en.summary: Six consecrated hosts hidden from an enemy attack during the Reconquista were reportedly found fused to their linen cloth, turned to visible flesh and blood.
en.body: During the Reconquista in 1239, Christian forces near Daroca, Spain, paused to celebrate Mass before an anticipated battle against a larger Moorish army, but a surprise attack forced the troops to break off suddenly while six hosts remained consecrated on the altar. Rather than risk the Blessed Sacrament being captured or desecrated, the priest is said to have wrapped the hosts in the linen corporal and hidden them inside a saddlebag before riding into battle, which the Christian forces went on to win. When the corporal was later retrieved, the six hosts were reportedly found fused permanently into the cloth itself, having visibly turned to flesh with blood staining the linen around them. The relics, known as the Corporales de Daroca, are enshrined in Daroca's collegiate church and remain one of Spain's most venerated Eucharistic relics, celebrated with a major annual festival.
